summary: Rapid connection migration resumes stale SSE snapshot: missing closing JSON brace and repeated assistant preamble
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that long-running SSE responses occasionally reattach to a previously closed conversation snapshot after a rapid client network migration. The resumed stream contains duplicated assistant preamble messages and the final JSON object is truncated (closing brace missing), causing client-side JSON.parse failures.

Impact:
- Customer-facing streaming sessions for AtlasDocs are intermittently producing invalid JSON payloads on reconnect (~0.8% of long streams observed for this customer).
- Clients see duplicate assistant system lines and then a JSONDecodeError when attempting to parse the final chunk; in their app this results in a visible truncated paragraph or missing final bullet items.

Environment:
- Customer environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east (vpc egress through transparent envoy sidecar).
- SDK/Client: atlasdocs-js v2.14.1 using EventSource (SSE) with automatic reconnect.
- Affected model: redwood-open-rlhf-v1, typical sequence length 1k-3k tokens.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Open SSE stream and request a ~2k token completion.
2) During generation, simulate rapid network migration (cellular -> wifi) or trigger a transparent proxy rebind on the client path (we reproduced using an envoy reconfigure / conn-rebind).
3) Client reconnects and sends resume request referencing last acknowledged offset.
4) Server resumes stream but emits an earlier assistant preamble and then continues; final JSON payload ends abruptly without the closing '}' or final newline.

Observed behaviour:
- Duplicate assistant preamble lines ("assistant: ... [system]" block) inserted immediately after resume.
- Final chunk truncated: last bytes end with '..."choices": [{"delta": {"content": "..."}}]' (missing closing brackets/braces).
- Client-side JSON.parse throws and client drops the last paragraph.

Expected behaviour:
- Resume should continue from the latest committed KV snapshot for the active session, not a stale snapshot.
- No duplicate system/assistant preamble. All emitted JSON objects must be well-formed and terminate with proper braces and delimiters.

Temporary workaround (customer):
- Increase client-side resume verification: if parse fails, fall back to re-request full non-streamed completion. Not ideal due to increased cost.
- Customer downgraded auto-reconnect to add a 300ms jitter which reduced reproduction frequency.

Logs / snippets:
- Worker logs (redacted):
  [2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] conn-id=ab12 rebind from 10.11.1.5 -> 10.23.4.1; session=atlas-72; kv-snap=2026-03-10T14:01:08Z
  [2026-03-10T14:03:21Z] resume-request offset=48712 last-ack=48712
  [2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] resume-applied snap=2026-03-09T23:58:12Z (stale)
  [2026-03-10T14:03:22Z] emit delta: assistant-preamble
  [2026-03-10T14:06:03Z] emit delta: final-chunk bytes=+512 truncated=true

Attached artifacts:
- customer-provided HAR of reconnect sequence, sample truncated payload, and SDK logs (attached to ticket).
steps_to_reproduce:
(see Description steps)
Reproducer notes:
- We used a Vagrant VM + controlled iptables to force a TCP migrate and envoys rebind. Repro rate ~40% under our test harness when forcing immediate client reconnect. Adding a 200-500ms client jitter reduced repro to <5%.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: race between conn-migration resume path and KV snapshot selection.
Findings so far:
- Worker logs show resume applied snapshot timestamp earlier than last-ack (snap=2026-03-09T23:58:12Z vs last-ack 2026-03-10T14:01:08Z) indicating stale snapshot selection during reattach.
- Edge-proxy (envoy) conn-handoff flow injects a rebind marker that our session-router treats as a new attach and occasionally performs a cold snapshot lookup instead of using in-memory committed offsets.
- The serving runtime will stream deltas taken from the snapshot; if the snapshot is stale, the preamble is emitted and token stream overlaps the previously delivered tokens.
- Truncated final chunk appears correlated with worker process performing an async flush while the resume was using a different buffer length; we saw an off-by-one length calculation in the delta-chunkizer for resumed streams (offending code path in runtime chunker module).

Next steps planned:
1) Add guard to session-router to prefer in-process committed offset if available when handling conn-handoff resume. (PR planned to edge-proxy/session-router boundary)
2) Add validation on emitted final JSON chunk to ensure object termination; if termination fails, trigger automatic re-emit of closing bytes or mark stream as failed and instruct client to retry.
3) Add targeted integration test simulating rapid conn migration with envoy rebind.
4) Coordinate with AtlasDocs to test patch in staging dedicated tenant.
